10#_: They are not included. Baer Heitev — and he wrote in Mishna Berurah in the name of Beit David: for a sick person whom the physician commanded to cook a whole chicken in water dripping from moist unsalted cheese that is nesyovei without salting the chicken in order to extract the water in an alembic — and this is his cure to drink that water — thus he should do to be saved from prohibition: roast the chicken first, and first cook the water dripping from the cheese and filter it, and take the clear water, and cook the chicken with that water in the alembic, and the sick person should drink, even though there is no danger.
11#_: And some forbid. Baer Heitev — see in Sefer HaMakri'a siman 33.
1#_: Only through cooking. Baer Heitev — the law of smoked, cooked, and fried — see below seif 6 and what is written there. And see in Mishbetzot: milk that was in a pot that was pickled overnight and afterward they cooked animal meat in it — forbidden in benefit; and although the pot absorbed through pickling, nevertheless it discharged afterward through cooking to the meat. And if the meat was fowl meat, it is forbidden in eating and one may not be lenient. And he wrote in Shevut Yaakov part 1 siman 61 regarding one who sent to ask a question of the decisor, and he forbade in benefit and the messenger discarded everything to loss; and afterward it became known that the decisor erred in a matter of mishnah — the decisor is exempt from paying since the decisor did not intend to harm, and even the messenger is exempt since he acted through an error in ruling. And he wrote in Noda BiYehuda siman 29: liver that was fried in forbidden butter is forbidden — not to speak of roasted liver that no longer discharges, it is nevertheless forbidden on account of the fat prohibition; but even living liver is forbidden even according to Rashi for this reason — see there.
2#_: Permitted in cooking and benefit. Baer Heitev — and what he wrote in the name of Radbaz, and Peri Chadash challenged him; and in Sha'ar HaMitzvot of Rabbenu R' Chaim Vital, parashat Mishpatim, he wrote: I saw people stringent not to eat sucuk made from sweet reeds with meat, because craftsmen whiten it by mixing goat milk in it as is known; and I saw my teacher of blessed memory eat it with meat together — end of his words. And this is like Radbaz's words, except that Radbaz permitted even without water, for even though there is no sixty in the sucuk alone it is permitted because the milk diminishes through fire and the sucuk does not diminish; and on this Peri Chadash challenged: since at the beginning of boiling there is no sixty against the milk, etc. — and his words are astonishing, and he stood on them in Mishna Berurah. And one sage wrote to him to emend the word "but if they cooked" should read "even if they cooked," etc.; and in place of "or if there is in the water" should read "but if there is in the water," etc. — his intent is that just as in prohibition diminution does not help as below siman 90, so too in permission, since it remains in its substance it is considered significant; therefore even a new pot does not help; but where there is sixty, even in the pot the meat is permitted, for everything returned to become permitted — see there. And Mishna Berurah wrote that it is not comfortable for him, for a prohibition is different: from the moment of falling it is already forbidden, unlike if it diminished while still permitted — see there. And in my humble opinion Peri Chadash wrote well according to the sage's view, for also in permission, immediately at the beginning of boiling the sucuk absorbs taste of milk, and even though the milk itself afterward diminishes, nevertheless taste of milk in the sucuk did not cease — I shortened. And Mishna Berurah wrote that for practical law all this is unnecessary, for it is known that special boilers are used and they put water in the boilers and the milk is nullified, and one need not be stringent at all; and behold there is testimony that the holy rabbi the Ari of blessed memory ate the finest of the fine — see there.
3#_: But fish and locusts have no prohibition. Baer Heitev — see Kenesset HaGedolah that according to physicians there is danger also in fish with milk; and in Mor uKetzia siman 73 likewise in the name of Rabbenu Bachya; and see in Eliyah Rabba in Orach Chaim siman 173, who wrote on Kenesset HaGedolah's words: what he wrote — I have not seen people careful about this. And see in Kenesset HaGedolah that Mahari"t his teacher and also some rabbis would take between fish and cheese; and Mishna Berurah agreed that an error fell in Beit Yosef, and in place of milk it must read meat; and in our lands the common people cook fish with milk and are not careful at all. And regarding cooking fish in a meat vessel — whether sixty helps will be explained in siman 116.
4#_: And they are accustomed to make almond milk. Baer Heitev — see Kenesset HaGedolah that he inclined to permit what people practice in Kostel at a festive meal: after eating meat dishes they eat rice cooked in almond milk; they also practice eating vine leaves and cabbage stuffed with meat with almond milk — see there. And in Mishna Berurah he further wrote a leniency: since they do this only at a festive meal such as a wedding or circumcision, and they place them in fancy platters or at least in special beautiful platters in which one does not eat a regular dish, and they also place fruits and delicacies on the table — it is almost recognizable in its place and its time more than placing almonds, vine leaves, and cabbage; they have grounds to permit, since the filling is covered and is not recognizable in the platter — neither the meat nor the milk — only in his mouth does he sense it; there is no marit ayin here.
5#_: And it appears according to this that all the more so it is forbidden to cook. Baer Heitev — see Mishna Berurah that before the Acharonim the body of Rashba's responsum was not available, and now we merited his words; and there in Chokhmat Adam siman 257 it is explained as Shach's words — see there.
6#_: Even though it is entangled. See Baer Heitev, and see what is written in the responsum there in the name of She'ilat Ya'avetz.
7#_:
One does not receive lashes. Baer Heitev — see Peri Chadash who wrote that in Yerushalmi Shabbat it was resolved: a question was asked whether smoked is considered cooking for Shabbat that one is liable — and likewise for basar b'chalav it is considered cooking; and in Peleti he rejected this, for one can say this is not the manner of cooking through heating in smoke. And see Mishna Berurah who challenged this: if so, why did the Rambam omit it regarding Shabbat? And see in Yeshuot Yaakov regarding Tiberias hot springs that he wrote it is because of a decree lest it be confused with derivatives of fire; and Mishna Berurah wrote that it is a Torah doubt as implied from chapter 5. And regarding roasted meat in milk, the view of Peri Chadash; and in Sefat Emet to Menachot general chapter 5 in the name of Tosafot Yom Tov, Mateh Yosef, and Peleti and Mishbetzot that it is forbidden from the Torah; and Mishna Berurah elaborated on this — see in Peri Chadash regarding roasted in a pot and frying whether included in cooking. And see in responsa Sha'ar Efrayim regarding butter that became forbidden through basar b'chalav because it was cooked in a meat Beit Yosef pot — whether permitted to kindle a Chanukah candle, because mitzvot were not given for benefit; and he also discussed roasted and frying. And I brought this in my responsa on the laws of Chanukah — see there.

And see in Sefat Emet regarding candles of milk that gentiles mix butter in time of distress — permitted to kindle, for frying forbidden from the Torah is permitted in benefit, and also there is no olive-size at one time; and see in Petichah to Peri Megadim he wondered on this — see Mishna Berurah who also wrote thus, that the principal matter here is as Peri Chadash that it is forbidden from the Torah, and there he brought from responsa Ohel Yosef who also permits. And Mishna Berurah elaborated and brings among them the Gaon Moharach Abualefia who forbade candles that were a mixture of butter and milk that Jews bought, and commanded to bury them, and great ones agreed with him; and so Mishna Berurah concludes there — see there, for Peri Megadim brought in the name of Mohar"m Shif who inclined that frying is permitted, and he concludes in Peri Megadim to permit; and Mishna Berurah wrote that the principal matter is as Peri Chadash and Mateh Yosef that frying is forbidden from the Torah — see there. And see in responsa Shevut Yaakov part 1 siman 60, where they challenged him on what he wrote in Sefat Emet his reasons for permission on account of frying, etc. — for it teaches that milk in milk has no prohibition of benefit; and he answered that certainly it is forbidden in benefit even for the Rambam, as is the view of Tosafot — see there. And see in Mishna Berurah that from the Rambam's commentary on the Mishnah in Keritot, in the wondrous note, it is clear that it is permitted in benefit; and see in Maggid Mishneh chapter 5 of Hilchot Yesodei HaTorah and in Sha'ar HaMelekh there; and see in Teshuvot HaTashbetz part 3 siman 295 who wrote that it is forbidden to cook butter alone to throw it as it is in a hot pan — one transgresses the negative commandment of cooking, for iruy in a kli rishon is like a kli rishon, and a negative commandment regarding benefit if he sells it, etc. — see there. And see in responsa Noda BiYehuda siman 29: liver fried in forbidden butter is forbidden — not to speak of roasted liver that does not discharge, it is nevertheless forbidden on account of fat prohibition; but even living liver is forbidden even according to Rashi for this reason. And what he wrote — and I already wrote what Peri Megadim brought in the name of Mohar"m Shif; and in Mishna Berurah he wrote one may not be lenient, for frying is like cooking and forbidden in benefit from the Torah — see there.
8#_: And therefore one should also forbid using the pots. Baer Heitev — and what he wrote: if so, how does he permit l'chatchila, etc. — see Tzemach Tzedek siman 98, who wrote that in truth one should not take ash to rinse utensils from the stove where they cook, but one takes ash from the oven where they bake bread and the like — see there. And in Magen Avraham end of seif 6 he wrote that he saw people are not careful about this and gave a reason that it is only a mere concern, and presumably all moisture in the ash has already been burned; it is also nullified in the water and gives noten taam lifgam through the ash; and rinsing eating utensils is only through iruy — and likewise see there. And see in Shulchan Aruch HaRav that one should be careful not to draw water in a meat vessel and afterward in a milk vessel, for sometimes they are dirty and there is no noten taam bar noten taam of permission; and see there that he wrote one should protest against those who do so.
9#_: And soft hooves are exempt. Baer Heitev — see in Shulchan Aruch HaRav that even hard bones are forbidden, not as implied in the responsum at the end of Magen Avraham that only marrow bones have a prohibition; and see in responsa at the end of his book: a hollow bone found inside a milk food, and there is doubt lest there was brain in it and it came out and mixed in the food — one should be stringent; and in a responsum at the end of Eliyah Rabba he disagreed and wrote to permit, for we do not establish a presumption of prohibition — see there. And it appears that those bones that are routinely known to have brain and it is their way to come out in cooking — one should be stringent in a small dish where there is no sixty.
